transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood, AE); Jordan Lee (Redwood, SE); Maya Patel (Lucid, Head of ML); Ethan Ross (Lucid, CTO); Priya Nair (Lucid, Lead Data Scientist)

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna run a 40-minute walkthrough of our eval and monitoring flow - prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B, and how Optimize ties in. Quick intros?
[00:18] Maya (Lucid): Hi, Maya here - I own ML infra for Lucid.
[00:23] Ethan (Lucid): Ethan, CTO, will listen for ops and infra questions.
[00:26] Priya (Lucid): Priya, data science, I'll share the prompt sets and expected metrics.
[00:31] Jordan (Redwood): Jordan, SE - I'll demo the console and run a small benchmark.
[00:36] Sofia (Redwood): Great. Quick agenda: 1) Console demo of eval dashboards; 2) how to upload prompt sets and label truth; 3) regression alerts and baselining; 4) A/B comparison and rollout recommendations; 5) next steps.
[01:05] Maya (Lucid): We're most interested in A/B and regression alerts - we've had drift after model swaps. We need a guardrail for hallucinations and NER drop.
[01:18] Sofia (Redwood): Totally. We'll show the alerting tied to your prompt suites and also per-route thresholds (latency/cost/quality).
[01:30] Jordan (Redwood): I'm going to share the screen - give me a sec. (screen share) Okay, this is the Redwood Console - "Evals" tab. Note, sometimes in notes it's referred to as "Redwood Eval" or even "Redwood Optima" in old decks so you'll see variations.
[01:58] Jordan (Redwood): Here is a prompt-set list - you can import YAML or CSV. Priya, you mentioned you keep A/B sets as CSVs?
[02:10] Priya (Lucid): Yes, we have 4k prompts across 10 intents - saved as CSV with labels and acceptance criteria.
[02:17] Jordan (Redwood): Perfect - you can map columns (prompt, expected, label, metadata). We also extract metadata for slicing: customer_segment, intent, channel.
[02:32] [screen flicker] Jordan (Redwood): Transcription note: "KV cache" sometimes shows as "K V cache" in the transcript. We support prefix/KV caching and you can see cache hit rates in the trace.
[02:46] Ethan (Lucid): A question on data residency - when we upload prompt sets with customer PII, where does that live?
[02:53] Sofia (Redwood): Hosted by default in Redwood tenants in your chosen region; for stricter needs we have Dedicated and Private with VPC/HSM integrations. We'll share SOC2, ISO docs - I know you asked for them.
[03:08] Priya (Lucid): For the eval metrics, what pre-built metrics are there? We use F1, exact-match, ROUGE for summarization.
[03:17] Jordan (Redwood): Built-ins include micro-F1, macro-F1, EM, ROUGE-L, BLEU, and custom script hooks. You can also plug an evaluation function via the API to compute business-specific KPIs.
[03:34] Jordan (Redwood): I'll run a quick demo: selected prompt set, run against two models (open-llama-v2 -> note: names may be different in product) and then a baseline.
[03:50] [04:05] Jordan (Redwood): Starting the run - you can choose sampling, temperature and token limits per-eval. Also you can set a tolerance band for numeric metrics; the regression alerts use a baseline window and an outlier detector.
[04:25] Maya (Lucid): How does the baseline work? Is it a moving window?
[04:31] Jordan (Redwood): It's configurable - baseline can be a fixed model snapshot or a rolling 14/30-day window. Alerts are triggered by statistic tests (we use bootstrap + practical delta thresholds). You can tune sensitivity per metric.
[05:02] Priya (Lucid): We need per-intent alerts - some intents are more critical.
[05:08] Jordan (Redwood): Yes, you can create slices and set different alert thresholds per slice. On the slices page we show error rate and metric deltas.
[05:28] Ethan (Lucid): Any integrations to Slack/PagerDuty?
[05:33] Sofia (Redwood): Yep - alert webhooks, Slack, PagerDuty, and email. We can also create weekly reports that go to the ML guild.
[05:48] [06:00] Jordan (Redwood): The run finished - here is the results page. Top-line summary: baseline micro-F1 0.93, new model 0.88, drift concentrated on "returns_intent" slice. We surfaced a hallucination score too (heuristic + detection model).
[06:25] Priya (Lucid): Oof - that's the intent that matters for refunds, 5% drop is material.
[06:30] Jordan (Redwood): We give per-prompt examples where the model failed - exportable as CSV for labelers. See the "failed examples" view.
[06:46] Maya (Lucid): Can we do A/B comparisons across two model flavors and then do partial rollouts?
[06:52] Jordan (Redwood): Absolutely - our rollout integration ties into the routing layer. You can do canaries (5/25/50) and specify fallback policies if quality drops below threshold; the console calculates expected cost impact for each rollout.
[07:12] [07:40] Jordan (Redwood): Here's an A/B chart - metrics over time for group A vs B. We can compute statistical significance and a delta table. For production we recommend running A/B on representative traffic; for offline you can replay logs.
[07:58] Priya (Lucid): For offline replays, what's the expected throughput? We have 20k requests/day in peak windows.
[08:08] Jordan (Redwood): In the hosted flow you can batch evals - Redwood Optimize suggests batching/granularity to reduce cost while preserving latency during online evals. For offline, we have a run harness that can process tens of thousands of prompts within an hour depending on model size and cluster.
[08:33] Maya (Lucid): You mentioned "Optimize" - what does that automate?
[08:38] Sofia (Redwood): Redwood Optimize is our recommendations engine - it looks at your workload, suggests quantization, batch sizes, model variants, and when to use cache/kv caching to save token cost. It also flags likely regressions if you upgrade to lower precision.
[08:58] Ethan (Lucid): Does Optimize recommend when to move from hosted to dedicated?
[09:03] Jordan (Redwood): It gives cost/latency projections for hosted vs dedicated for your workload and suggests an inflection point where reserved capacity makes sense.
[09:22] [09:40] Priya (Lucid): About alerts - can we get runbook links or auto-notes when an alert fires?
[09:46] Jordan (Redwood): Yes - the alert template supports runbook links, owner assignment, and a one-click snapshot export (prompts, responses, trace).
[10:00] Maya (Lucid): What about model-card metadata? We need a history of model versions and which training data was used.
[10:08] Sofia (Redwood): We store model artifacts and annotate versions. For Private installs we can integrate with your model registry. We'll share docs on model provenance.
[10:22] [10:40] Jordan (Redwood): I'm going to show the API flow - you can POST prompt-set, then POST /evals/run and poll a job; or use the SDK for async notifications.
[10:56] Jordan (Redwood): Example curl: curl -X POST /v1/evals -d '{"prompt_file": "s3://...", "metrics": ["micro_f1"] }' - note: in transcript braces get munged sometimes.
[11:12] Priya (Lucid): Do you support custom scoring code? We have a proprietary fuzzy match routine.
[11:19] Jordan (Redwood): Yes - code hooks let you run custom python scoring in a sandbox; results are stored as columns for slicing. Code artifacts are versioned.
[11:36] Ethan (Lucid): Any performance overhead for running custom scoring?
[11:40] Jordan (Redwood): There's a small compute cost since it runs in the scoring stage - we meter and surface cost. For heavy custom logic we recommend precomputing or running in a dedicated worker pool.
[12:02] [12:20] Jordan (Redwood): Next, regression alerts detail: you set baseline window, stat test, min sample, and suppressions. Alerts have a backfill option so you can retroactively evaluate.
[12:38] Maya (Lucid): Our main worry is false positives - historically we had noisy alerts.
[12:43] Sofia (Redwood): You can set a minimum effect size and use a two-stage test (trigger + confirm) to reduce noise. We also expose the raw p-values and confidence intervals so your SREs can tune.
[13:05] Priya (Lucid): Show me examples of false positives - how do I triage?
[13:12] Jordan (Redwood): In the alert detail you can see the contributing prompts and the delta per-slice; you can mark an alert as false-positive and add it to a suppression list for the slice/model combo.
[13:30] [14:00] Jordan (Redwood): I'm going to open the "rollback" playbook - when a regression passes threshold, you can auto-roll back to previous model and open a ticket.
[14:15] Ethan (Lucid): That integration is critical - we want a safety net for customer-facing flows.
[14:20] Sofia (Redwood): Exactly - we can also trigger traffic shift to a more conservative model variant based on confidence score.
[14:38] Maya (Lucid): For the A/B analysis, does Redwood do hypothesis testing across multiple metrics? We care about business metric composite.
[14:46] Jordan (Redwood): Yes - multi-metric tests and a customizable scoring function; you can weigh metrics to produce a composite score and do sequential testing.
[15:05] Priya (Lucid): How are prompts labeled for multi-turn? Some of our flows are multi-turn with memory.
[15:12] Jordan (Redwood): We support multi-turn captures; you can store conversation context and label at the final turn or per-turn. The console shows turn-level breakdowns. KV cache behavior is surfaced in traces so you can see where past context was reused.
[15:38] [16:00] Jordan (Redwood): We'll do a short live A/B: run prompt set across model A (current) and model B (candidate) - quick run.
[16:18] Jordan (Redwood): Run started; progress bar... about 4 minutes for a 2k prompt set on this cluster. For your 4k it will take longer but still acceptable.
[16:45] [19:00] Jordan (Redwood): Results are in - here's example failure clusters. You can group failures by error type (hallucination, incorrect-slot, latency timeouts).
[19:21] Priya (Lucid): Can we link to our internal ticketing system so failures create JIRA items?
[19:27] Sofia (Redwood): Yes, webhook integration to create tickets with context payload.
[19:40] Ethan (Lucid): Security again - are eval logs encrypted at rest and who can access them?
[19:46] Jordan (Redwood): Logs are encrypted; RBAC controls restrict access. You can set retention and export policies. For Dedicated/Private we can support your KMS/HSM.
[20:04] Maya (Lucid): Curious about cost for frequent runs - if we want nightly regressions across all intents, what's the ballpark?
[20:11] Sofia (Redwood): Depends on model size and batching. Redwood Optimize will recommend a cost-aware profile - for example, use a quantized 8-bit variant for nightly detection and full-precision for canaries. We'll send a sample pricing calc with your prompt counts.
[20:40] [21:00] Jordan (Redwood): Quick note on imperfect transcriptions: sometimes product names like "Redwood Optimize" show as "Redwood Optima" in auto notes; ignore that.
[21:10] Priya (Lucid): Is there a way to import our existing eval history? We have 6 months in-house.
[21:17] Jordan (Redwood): Importable via S3 or API - we can backfill history to compute proper baselines. There's a mapping step for legacy metrics.
[21:36] Maya (Lucid): On the A/B results, do you provide sample-level delta explanations?
[21:42] Jordan (Redwood): Yes - for each prompt we show the two responses side-by-side, with token-level diffs and a confidence delta. You can tag examples for relabeling or to seed a targeted prompt set.
[22:03] Priya (Lucid): About the relabeling workflow - can we have our labeling team operate from the console?
[22:09] Jordan (Redwood): Yes - native labeler UI, assign tasks, and sync back results. Labeler actions become new truth columns in the dataset.
[22:26] Ethan (Lucid): If an alert is noisy, is there an audit trail to see who muted it?
[22:31] Sofia (Redwood): Yes audit logs show who changed thresholds or muted alerts; these are exportable for compliance.
[22:50] [23:10] Jordan (Redwood): Demo: creating a regression alert - selecting baseline window, metric, slice and setting Slack webhook. (pause) Alert created.
[23:28] Maya (Lucid): Nice. How granular can the slices be?
[23:33] Jordan (Redwood): Very granular - any metadata dimension or combination thereof, including custom tags in prompt metadata.
[23:50] Priya (Lucid): For the pilot, we want nightly runs, slice-level alerts, and auto-ticketing to JIRA. What's the timeline?
[23:58] Sofia (Redwood): We usually provision trial org within 24-48 hours, then a benchmark run and a two-week calibration period. For your needs, 6-week pilot with dedicated SE engagement seems right.
[24:20] [24:40] Jordan (Redwood): I'll attach an example eval run and export the CSV of failed examples now. (exports)
[24:55] Priya (Lucid): We'll need the export for our labeling team.
[25:02] Jordan (Redwood): Sending link in chat - note: shared links expire per security policy but we can arrange S3 transfer.
[25:18] Maya (Lucid): Any limitations on custom scoring runtimes?
[25:24] Jordan (Redwood): Sandbox limits CPU/memory; for heavy jobs we recommend dedicated scoring cluster. We'll surface estimate in the cost calc.
[25:40] [26:00] Sofia (Redwood): I'll recap next steps at the end but Jordan - can you confirm the items you need from Lucid?
[26:09] Jordan (Redwood): Sure: sample prompt sets (CSV/YAML), a subset of labeled truth (if possible), and A/B mapping CSV. Also access to a representative replay log for traffic shape.
[26:28] Priya (Lucid): We can share the prompt ZIP and labeled subset by 7/14.
[26:34] Sofia (Redwood): Great. We'll prep the trial org and schedule the benchmark.
[26:45] [27:00] Jordan (Redwood): Quick show of the Optimize recommendations: here's a suggested quantization profile and batch size for your typical sequence lengths (mean 120 tokens). It predicts 40% token-cost reduction with 8-bit quant and batching of 16.
[27:28] Maya (Lucid): 40% is substantial. What's the expected quality delta?
[27:33] Jordan (Redwood): For similar workloads we saw <1.5% micro-F1 delta, but we run regression checks first. Optimize flags cases likely to degrade.
[27:50] Ethan (Lucid): If degradation occurs, can we isolate which intents are sensitive?
[27:55] Jordan (Redwood): Yes - slice-level deltas are part of the Optimize report.
[28:10] [28:30] Priya (Lucid): Any pre-built eval templates for ecommerce intents (returns, refunds, order-status)?
[28:36] Jordan (Redwood): We have starter prompt sets and templates for common verticals; we'll share the retail pack.
[28:50] Maya (Lucid): Great. A few compliance Qs: SSO, RBAC, and retention policies?
[28:57] Sofia (Redwood): We support SAML/SSO, fine-grained RBAC, and configurable retention. Security pack will include details.
[29:15] [29:30] Jordan (Redwood): Back to A/B significance - the console shows p-values, confidence intervals, and an automatic recommendation for whether to promote. You can also require business-metric thresholds before rollout.
[29:48] Priya (Lucid): Can we do model-variant routing by confidence score?
[29:54] Jordan (Redwood): Yes - route to conservative variant if confidence < threshold, or fall back to prior model.
[30:08] Maya (Lucid): For the pilot, what level of Redwood involvement is included? SE hours?
[30:14] Sofia (Redwood): Pilot includes SE hours for onboarding and a benchmark run; beyond that we can propose an engagement plan.
[30:28] [30:50] Jordan (Redwood): I'll demo the alert timeline - here's one we set earlier: it lists triggers, affected slices, and remediation suggestions. You can export a notebook to reproduce the failing examples.
[31:12] Priya (Lucid): Repro notebooks sound useful.
[31:20] Jordan (Redwood): They capture the eval config, model versions, and random seeds if used.
[31:36] Ethan (Lucid): Any audit/attestation for calls to third-party models?
[31:42] Sofia (Redwood): We log model endpoints and versions. For external closed-source models we capture provider metadata; for Private installs you manage the model registry.
[31:58] [32:20] Jordan (Redwood): Performance note - when doing large evals we use dynamic kernel selection and continuous batching in the runtime; in the UI we show expected QPS and tail latency distribution.
[32:44] Maya (Lucid): Will you share the runtime performance whitepaper?
[32:48] Sofia (Redwood): Yes - will include kernel selection and caching behavior docs.
[33:05] [33:30] Priya (Lucid): If we onboard, what's the SLA for the Dedicated tier?
[33:36] Sofia (Redwood): Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include the SLA appendix in the enterprise pack.
[33:50] Ethan (Lucid): Can we run on-prem later?
[33:53] Sofia (Redwood): Yes - Redwood Private supports on-prem with a customer-managed control plane.
[34:10] [34:30] Jordan (Redwood): Demo wrap-up - I exported examples, set a sample regression alert, and kicked off the canary simulation.
[34:45] Priya (Lucid): This looks promising. A couple of small asks: better false-positive suppression UX and a way to auto-generate slice names from metadata ingestion.
[34:58] Jordan (Redwood): Noted - we'll record that feedback.
[35:10] Sofia (Redwood): Recap of next steps - we'll send pilot pricing and security docs, provision trial org, Jordan will run a baseline benchmark w/ Lucid data, and we'll schedule a follow-up on 2026-07-17.
[35:28] Maya (Lucid): Sounds good.
[35:33] Ethan (Lucid): Thanks everyone.
[35:37] Priya (Lucid): Thanks.
[35:40] Sofia (Redwood): Thanks - we'll follow up in email with the links and docs.
[35:50] [End 15:42 local 42:00 elapsed]
